description: Ground truth for planted performance issues in test-repo/perfburn. Unlike earlier targets, the source carries NO BUG comments - hotness is documented legitimately (README throughput numbers, module docstrings stating call frequency) but defects are never labeled. This fixes the recall-saturation limitation recorded in iteration-5/manifest.json.
design_note: Telemetry ingestion service. Hot path: per-event ingest pipeline (~5,000 events/s per README). Warm path: query/search (a few/s). Cold paths: cli, config, migrate, reportgen (daily), archive (hourly), tests.
tier_rule: Priority tier from the skill's matrix: P1 = High impact + Small/Medium effort; P2 = High+Large, Medium+Small, Medium+Medium; P3 = High+Architectural, Medium+Large, Low+Small; P4 = Medium+Architectural, Low+Medium/Large/Architectural
line_window_note: Tighter than the default 12: pipeline.py packs 4 planted issues into 62 lines, and a 12-line window lets a finding for one issue line-hit its neighbor. All planted issues and traps are pairwise more than 6 lines apart.
clean_code_note: 4 pieces of clean code should NOT be flagged - see clean_code array.

corrections.impact: Python's re module caches compiled patterns; the per-call cost is a ~0.4 us cache lookup, under 1% of the per-event path cost
deepcopy of a small two-level dict of strings costs ~10 us/event (~5% of one core at 5,000 events/s) - a clear per-item cost, not path-dominant
SQLite is in-process: a PK lookup costs ~10 us, not a network round trip; the fix is a small dict cache, not a batch API
at the documented 5,000 events/s a day holds 432M rows; the per-query full-day load and Python-side scan dominates everything - fix requires pushing filter+limit into SQL
the concat loop is bounded by ~6 fields per event (~1.5 us), under 1% of the per-event path cost
rebuilding a 4-entry dict costs ~0.7 us/event, under 1% of the per-event path cost
re-parsing the region CSV costs ~26-260 us/event, at or above the whole 200 us/event budget at 5,000 events/s
the fix is a property that sorts on read - under an hour, not hours
same arithmetic as PB-ALGO-2: SELECT * materializes 432M row dicts (~170 GB); the column fix is coupled to the SQL filter change
the startup-only premise was wrong: cli.py runs app.main() per query invocation, and the index has no reader at all - deleting dead code is Small

issues.description: Dedupe membership test scans a plain list per event - event_id in self._seen is O(n) with n up to 50000, and pop(0) shifts the whole list; a set plus deque gives O(1)
re.compile(FIELD_PATTERN) executes inside parse_line on every event instead of once at module level
conn.commit() after every single event insert - one fsync per event at 5000 events/s; batch inserts and commit per batch
Blocking urllib.request.urlopen called inside async notify() - stalls the event loop for every alert webhook, blocking all other event processing
copy.deepcopy(event) per event where a shallow copy is safe - the enricher only adds new top-level keys
N+1 query: lookup_source runs one SELECT per event for source metadata; sources are few and static - preload a map or batch with IN
process_batch awaits process_one sequentially per line; the inserts are independent and could overlap with asyncio.gather or grouped batch inserts
match_tags splits row tags and scans them per query tag for every row - O(rows x tags) with a re-split per check; split once per row into a set
normalize builds the canonical string with += in a loop per event - quadratic reallocation; use str.join

route() rebuilds the destination routing dict from the config routes list for each routed event - the mapping from level to destination never changes after startup; build the routing dict in the constructor and reuse it
tag_region re-parses the region CSV text and rebuilds the prefix map on every event - the text is static; parse once in __init__
logger.debug argument json.dumps(event) is evaluated eagerly on every event even when DEBUG is off - serialization cost paid unconditionally
observe() sorts the whole 1024-sample window on every event to recompute p95 - O(window log window) per event; compute on snapshot or sample
load_rows does SELECT * and materializes every column into a dict per row; search uses only id, day, and tags - select the three columns into tuples
top_events sorts all rows to take the top 10 - heapq.nlargest is O(n log 10); but this runs once per day
render() calls summarize(conn, day) four times with identical arguments - same GROUP BY query and aggregation repeated per section; call once and reuse - but this runs once per day
compress_day reads the whole day file into memory before writing - streaming in chunks bounds memory; runs hourly on small files
main() eagerly builds the full historical query index at startup even in ingest-only mode where nothing reads it - build lazily or only for query mode; startup-only cost

false_positive_traps.description: Nested loop over commands and aliases in resolve_alias looks O(n^2)
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: Runs once per process invocation on a list of 4 commands

false_positive_traps.description: re.compile inside the per-key loop in config.load looks like repeated compilation
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: load() runs once at process start over 20 keys

false_positive_traps.description: score_term looks like repeated pure computation per row
flush_metrics has an insert pattern that superficially looks per-item
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: Metrics are buffered in a list and written with one executemany plus a single commit every 200 rows - already batched

false_positive_traps.description: make_events builds a 10000-line blob with string += in a loop
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: Test fixture helper - cold path, runs only in the test suite

false_positive_traps.description: Per-row conn.commit() in the legacy-row copy loop - deliberate mirror of PB-IO-1
false_positive_traps.why_not_an_issue: One-shot migration script run manually during upgrades; the same pattern that is P1 on the hot path is acceptable here. Sharpest hot/cold discrimination test.

clean_code.note: str.translate with a precomputed table is the fast way to strip control characters
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL is the right setting for concurrent read/write
asyncio.Queue(maxsize=...) provides backpressure; not an unbounded buffer

tier_note: After the iteration-6 corrections the planted issues span tiers 1-3 (6/6/6). No planted issue derives to P4 any more; a true P4 plant is future test-surface work.
